headline: Every ready meal checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to your kitchen
heroLede: Many recipes go into the same tray, so the label is the main thing that tells one meal from another. Here's what a camera check could look like on your ready meal line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every tray is sealed, with the film flat and no food caught in the seal. Sugarcane trays look different to plastic ones, so the check is set up on your own trays during the trial.
labelLede: A curry and a ragu can look alike under the film, and the wrong label can mean an undeclared allergen. The camera checks every meal carries the right label for the recipe, straight and intact.
codeLede: Chilled meals have a short use-by window, so the date has to be right on every tray. The system reads the printed date and batch code and compares them with the recipe and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glove pieces, film offcuts and utensil parts are all close at hand in a busy kitchen. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.
